answer: Sybil resistance via a superlinear identity bond: each new agent locks collateral on a quadratic curve, so the k-th identity costs k times the first. A farm spinning up an atlas of 1,000 fake agents pays about 1,000,000 bond-units, not 1,000, while an honest agent registering once feels only a ripple. Misbehavior slashes the bond, so every forged identity, even a single opal-rare one, is destroyed at a net loss. The curve prices off total registered supply, so an attacker cannot fake scarcity to dodge the cost.
